text.title: PR Pattern Mining For Feedback Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for the feedback report: the corpus with its window, counts and exact query (and the insufficient-sample gate at 20 PRs / 100 comments), the declared team or mentee scope, at most five top patterns each phrased as a code behaviour with before and after, recurrence across 3 PRs and 2 reviewers with at least 3 comment URLs, a frequency x cost score, a baseline and a re-measure date, the single automation-gap item for formatter-coverable comments, suggested rules with an enforcement channel, and the owner's check before sharing. Validator: `scripts/validate-pr-pattern-mining-for-feedback.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the schema cannot express and the reviewer checks by hand: `corpus.sufficient_sample` is true exactly when `merged_prs >= 20` and `review_comments >= 100` (r-corpus-window-and-query-stated); `top_patterns` are the five highest `score` values where `score = count x cost` on the stated `ranking_basis`, and everything below them is in `appendix_patterns` (r-ranked-by-frequency-times-cost); every `suggested_rules[].pattern_id` names a `top_patterns` entry, and a suggestion with no channel lives in `notes` (r-suggested-rule-names-enforcement-channel); when `previous_report_url` is set, every top pattern carries `delta_vs_previous` computed with the same `query` (r-baseline-and-remeasure-per-pattern); `automation_gap.comments_excluded` equals the number of formatter-coverable comments removed from all pattern counts (r-formatter-covered-comments-excluded).

example.note: Subject violations: nine PRs and 41 comments from a ten-day window declared sufficient, fetched by no reproducible query (r-corpus-window-and-query-stated); a trait-phrased pattern with two PRs, one reviewer and one URL (r-pattern-phrased-as-code-behaviour, r-pattern-requires-recurrence); an import-order pattern in the top list instead of one automation-gap item (r-formatter-covered-comments-excluded); a guideline rule with no reason the earlier channels do not apply, still active after three cycles without a drop (r-suggested-rule-names-enforcement-channel, r-baseline-and-remeasure-per-pattern); per-author counts in a team-scoped report (r-per-person-scope-declared-and-consented); and a report shared by the agent with no owner check.

antipattern.description: A top or appendix pattern with fewer than 3 `distinct_prs`, fewer than 2 `distinct_reviewers` (or 1 reviewer under 5 PRs), or fewer than 3 `comment_urls`; a corpus under 20 PRs or 100 comments with `sufficient_sample` true or with any suggested rule.
antipattern.reason: r-pattern-requires-recurrence, r-corpus-window-and-query-stated: three comments from one bad week are a bad week.

antipattern.description: A `behaviour` naming an attitude or a person (careless, lazy, does not think, lacks rigour), or a pattern without `before_example` and `after_example`.
antipattern.reason: r-pattern-phrased-as-code-behaviour: feedback about the person changes morale, not the code.

antipattern.description: A pattern with `formatter_coverable` true anywhere in `top_patterns`, or formatter-coverable comments counted instead of collapsed into `automation_gap` with a tool and config change; `ranking_basis` missing.
antipattern.reason: r-formatter-covered-comments-excluded, r-ranked-by-frequency-times-cost: raw count promotes whatever is easiest to comment on.

antipattern.description: A suggested rule with no `channel`, a linter or CI channel without `channel_id`, a later channel without `why_not_earlier_channels`, or a channel-less suggestion outside `notes`.
antipattern.reason: r-suggested-rule-names-enforcement-channel: a guideline in a wiki is enforced by whoever remembers it.

antipattern.description: `per_author_counts_listed` true under `team` scope, or a `mentee` scope where the mentee is not the primary reader or the evaluation use is unstated.
antipattern.reason: r-per-person-scope-declared-and-consented: a leaderboard turns reviewers into people whose comments count against colleagues.

antipattern.description: A top pattern without `baseline_count` and `remeasure_date`; a report with `previous_report_url` and no `delta_vs_previous`; a rule with `cycles_without_drop` of 2 or more still `new` or `active`.
antipattern.reason: r-baseline-and-remeasure-per-pattern: a rule that produced no drop is noise in the style guide.

antipattern.description: `review.shared_by_agent` true, or `checked_and_shared` with no owner and check date.
antipattern.reason: Human checkpoint in `03-failure-modes.xml`: the report owner checks the cited URLs and the scope before the report is shared.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
Feedback report skeleton with the same sections and field names.
